definitions.explanation: An activity, typically done at night, where participants walk through a dark, scary location (such as a graveyard or forest) to test their bravery.

examples.japanese: {肝試|きもだめ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To do a test of courage.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦キャンプ→キャンプ：03837_kyanpu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肝試|きもだめ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We did a test of courage at summer camp.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{墓地|ぼち}→墓地：15232_bochi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{肝試|きもだめ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦したら→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{怖|こわ}くて→怖い：00864_kowai⟧⟦{泣|な}いて→泣く：00655_naku⟧しまった。
examples.english: When I did a test of courage with friends in a graveyard at night, I got so scared that I cried.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{肝試|きもだめ}し is a classic Japanese summer activity, especially popular at school camps, community events, and among groups of friends. Participants typically walk through a dark area (a forest, abandoned building, or graveyard) where others may be hiding to scare them. It is closely associated with the Japanese summer tradition of telling ghost stories (⟦{怪談|かいだん}→怪談：12608_kaidan⟧).

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{肝|きも}→肝：10796_kimo⟧ (liver/courage) + ⟦{試|ため}し→試し：03410_tameshi⟧ (test). In traditional Japanese thought, the liver was considered the seat of courage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肝試|きもだめ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to do a test of courage
- {肝試|きもだめ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go on a test of courage
- ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{肝試|きもだめ}し: summer test of courage
